key_insight: A systematic comparison of vision–language–action (VLA) models reveals which architectural and training choices most strongly determine real-world robotic performance, enabling targeted design of generalist robot agents.
problem_solved: Clarifies which components and training strategies actually matter when building VLA models for robots, resolving ambiguity about where to invest effort to achieve robust, general-purpose robot behavior.
method: Empirical comparison and controlled ablations across representative VLA model designs (perception backbone, language module, policy head, training regimen).
Evaluation on diverse embodied tasks and metrics to link model choices to downstream robotic capabilities (sim-to-real and in-simulation benchmarks).
Analysis of data sources and finetuning strategies (instruction tuning, multimodal pretraining, grounding) to rank their effect sizes.
impact: Provides clear, evidence-based guidance for researchers and engineers on which model components and training practices yield the biggest gains for generalist robots, reducing wasted effort and accelerating deployment.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram breaking a VLA model into perception, language, and action modules with arrows showing information flow.
Bar chart or ranked ablation plot showing relative importance of design/training factors (e.g., multimodal pretraining, instruction tuning, policy capacity).
Task performance heatmap across multiple embodied tasks to illustrate generalization vs specialization trade-offs.
Pipeline infographic showing data sources → pretraining → finetuning → deployment (with icons for simulation, real robot, language data)
paper_title: What matters in building vision–language–action models for generalist robots
paper_authors: Xinghang Li, Peiyan Li, Long Qian, Minghuan Liu, Dong Wang
